images.title: Lunch money, five days
images.purpose: Show that the same amount is spent on each of five days, so the total is built from five equal parts.
images.composition: One row of five identical canteen trays centred on the page, with a lot of white space above and below.
exact_structure: Five identical rounded rectangles (trays) in one horizontal row, evenly spaced, dark outline, light teal #0072B2 fill.
Each tray holds one amber #E69F00 coin-shaped circle marked with the same amount.
A small label above each tray, left to right: Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 4, Day 5.
A reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded box at the right end of the row, after Day 5, holding a question mark and the text Total?
rejection: any coin showing an amount other than ₹25
a tray left without a coin
images.takeaway: The same ₹25 is spent each day, five times over.
images.description: Five lunch trays in a row, each with a ₹25 coin, and a box asking for the total.
images.context: Shown beside the opening scene before the expression is written.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to count the days and the coins and say what the total might look like.

image_decisions.why: The hook needs a clear picture of five equal daily spends.
